Fireworks serverless is usually the simpler choice for bursty or uncertain traffic because you pay for input, cached-input, and output tokens. Fireworks on-demand can be cheaper when one or more dedicated GPUs stay sufficiently busy, but the answer depends on the GPU shape, model throughput, replica schedule, cache share, service tier, and whether the workload is eligible for batch processing. Fireworks describes serverless as per-token and on-demand deployments as per-GPU-time billing; the current pricing page lists H100 and H200 capacity at $8.00 per GPU hour, or $0.134 per GPU minute, before any region premium. Fireworks’ deployment documentation describes the option as cost-effective at scale and says the deployment is billed by GPU-second. The same page lists lower latency, higher throughput, broader model selection, and custom-model support as reasons to choose a deployment, but those benefits do not turn into a cost saving unless your measured utilization supports them. Fireworks AI is a Redwood City inference provider that serves open-weight and closed models per-token on shared serverless capacity, by GPU-second on On Demand deployments, or via Reserved Throughput — dollars-per-minute reservations backed by a 99.9% uptime SLA. highlights:
# What an H100 costs per hour, by provider

Prices checked on each vendor's pricing page in November 2026. Hourly equivalents for per-second and per-minute billing are our own calculation.

AI Tools Hub Editorial · published 2026-11-01 · updated 2026-11-01

## H100 hourly rates

| Provider | Form | Per hour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Together AI | Cluster, preemptible | $1.99 |
| Together AI | Cluster, reserved 3–180 days | $3.19–$3.69 |
| Together AI | Cluster, on demand | $3.99 |
| Modal | Per-second (H100 SXM5) | ~$3.95 |
| Together AI | Dedicated inference | $5.49 |
| Replicate | H100 | $5.49 |
| Baseten | Dedicated deployment | ~$6.50 |
| Fireworks | On demand H100 80GB | $8.00 |

Not strictly like for like — clusters you operate yourself, dedicated inference includes the serving layer.

## Three bands

Preemptible at $1.99 suits work that can be interrupted: batch embedding, offline evaluation, overnight training. You must build the resume logic yourself.

Reserved suits predictable load and saves roughly 20% against on demand. On demand suits experiments and unknown load, and is where you should start.

## Check before comparing rates

- Whether the GPU is actually available
- Whether pinning a region adds a premium — Fireworks charges 1.5x
- Separate storage and egress charges
- Minimum terms and cancellation

results.title: Priced per TB/s, the H200 beats the H100 at 6 of 7 providers | InferPrice
highlights:
# Priced per TB/s, the H200 beats the H100 at 6 of 7 providers

2026-11-02 · GPUs Cost Inference 

Decode runs out of memory bandwidth before compute. We priced H100, H200 and B200 per TB/s-hour from NVIDIA specs and 2026-10-30 list prices.

An H200 has exactly as much compute as an SXM H100 and usually rents for more, so on a FLOPS spreadsheet it never makes sense. The H200 vs H100 cost per token question turns on a different column: the H200 moves 4.8 TB/s out of memory against the H100's 3.35, and decode spends its time waiting on memory. Memory is also what the industry is short of: TechCrunch reports that Samsung used its Q2 earnings call to say the shortage worsens in 2027 and stays tight until at least 2028.

So we priced that column, using our GPU table for 2026-10-30.

...

## The table that follows from that

Same provider, same day, SXM H100 against H200 (Vast, Lambda and Baseten list no H200, so they're out):

| Provider | H100 $/h | H200 $/h | H100 $/TB/s-h | H200 $/TB/s-h | B200 $/TB/s-h |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fireworks | 8.00 | 8.00 | 2.39 | 1.67 | 1.62 |
| CoreWeave | 6.16 | 6.31 | 1.84 | 1.31 | 1.07 |
| Nebius | 4.50 | 5.40 | 1.34 | 1.13 | 1.06 |
| Modal | 3.95 | 4.54 | 1.18 | 0.95 | 0.78 |
| DeepInfra | 2.90 | 3.49 | 0.87 | 0.73 | 0.61 |
| RunPod | 3.99 | 5.29 | 1.19 | 1.10 | 1.00 |
| Together AI | 3.99 | 5.99 | 1.19 | 1.25 | 1.02 |

The break-even is 4.8 / 3.35, so the H200 wins per TB/s whenever it costs under 1.43 times the H100. Together AI, at 1.50 times, is the one provider here where it loses. The B200 wins at all seven, and it's the cheapest row at each.

The cheap-looking row is the trap. RunPod's PCIe H100 lists at $2.89, but NVIDIA's product brief gives that card a peak of 2,000 GB/s, so you pay $1.45 per TB/s-hour: more than RunPod's SXM H100, H200 or B200.

Memory size isn't in the table. An H100 holds 80 GB, an H200 141 GB and a B200 180 GB, before any KV cache. If your model doesn't fit, the honest comparison is two cheaper cards against one bigger one, and the per-TB/s number won't settle that.

Peak bandwidth isn't sustained bandwidth. NVIDIA's figures are peaks ("up to 8TB/s" for the B200). That paper's memory ceiling for its card is 1.63 TB/s, under half the SXM figure, though it describes an unusual 64 GB H100, so don't treat that as a discount rate.

...

DeepInfra and Fireworks list their H100 only as 80 GB, so we assumed SXM. If either is a PCIe card the H200 wins by more, so the count holds.

We ran nothing on these GPUs. The tokens-per-second figures are bounds from published specs. Discounts reorder the table too: on Together AI's 91 to 180 day reserved rates ($3.19 and $3.99) the H200 costs 1.25 times the H100 and wins, though its preemptible rates stay at 1.50 times. Some of these rates only come in bulk or as a managed service, such as CoreWeave's 8-GPU instances and DeepInfra's dedicated deployments, so compare within a row, not across providers.

### GPU rental rates moved in October: marketplace floors hold, hyperscaler blocks jump

Two pricing events affect the break-even tables below. Nebius's published rates show on-demand increases of 17 to 21 percent on October 1, 2026, putting the H100 at $4.50 per GPU-hour (H200 $5.40, B200 $8.50, B300 $9.50), its second increase since May. AWS repriced EC2 Capacity Blocks on October 7, 2026: the P5 (H100) block now runs $5.970 per GPU-hour, up 15 percent from $5.191, and P6-B300 reaches $16.146 per GPU-hour.

The marketplace end of the market barely moved: the cheapest posted H100 held near $1.80 per hour on October 21, while the cross-provider median sat at $3.75 per GPU-hour across the 57 providers and 456 price points tracked by GetDeploying, a 90-day trend it reports as flat. That spread is now the widest part of the market: the $1.80 floor in the table and AWS's $5.970 capacity block describe the same GPU. Source →

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
# Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16

Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

What it does to the board when it lands: Lambda's B200 at $6.69 is currently the cheapest verified HGX B200 instance rate we list from a self-serve cloud; at $7.69 it would sit above RunPod Community's $5.98 marketplace rate and just below RunPod Secure's $7.99. Its H100 at $4.59 would remain above the board's best H100 SXM offer (TensorDock, from $2.25 at an 8-GPU minimum) but move Lambda from the middle of the H100 pack toward its top. Around-the-clock, the announced rises add about $730 a month per B200, $438 per H100 and $292 per A100 80GB on a 730-hour month.
